plan: Since this ascending-clock mechanism with sealed exit bids functions like a second-price auction, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever the price is below my value (profitable) and don't overpay when it's above. There's no incentive to shade or inflate my bid since I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, if I win. Therefore, I will bid $3, my true value.

Since this is effectively a second-price auction (the clock ends when only one bidder remains, and the winner pays the second-highest bid), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (my value exceeds the price) and never overpay, since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win. There's no incentive to shade my bid up or down in this mechanism.

Since this is effectively a second-price auction (the clock stops when only one bidder remains, and the winner pays the exit price of the second-highest bidder), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. This ensures I win whenever profitable (value > price paid) and avoid losses when the competition's value exceeds mine. Bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies.
